title: An Automated Method to Perform The In Vitro Micronucleus Assay using Multispectral Imaging Flow Cytometry
protocol: Prepare 565 mL of 1x RPMI culture medium.
Add 5 mL of MEM non-essential amino acids (100x) to the medium.
Add 5 mL of sodium pyruvate (100 mM) to the medium.
Add 5 mL of penicillin-streptomycin-glutamine (100x) to the medium.
Add 50 mL of fetal bovine serum (FBS) to the medium in a 500 mL bottle.
Store the prepared medium at 2-8 °C.
Heat the medium to 37 °C prior to use with TK6 cells.
Thaw 1 mL of TK6 cells stored at -80 °C in DMSO in 10 mL of medium.
Centrifuge the thawed cells at 200 x g for 8 min.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Transfer the cells to 50 mL of media.
Incubate the transferred cells at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Culture the cells to a concentration of ~7-8 x 10^5 cells/mL in 100 mL volume.
Dissolve a full 2 mg bottle of Mitomycin C in 10 mL of sterile water to achieve a stock concentration of 200 µg/mL.
Store the Mitomycin C solution at 4°C for up to three months.
Prepare dilutions on experiment day by mixing to achieve concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, and 5.0 µg/mL in sterile water.
For Colchicine, dissolve a full bottle in 10 mL of sterile water to achieve an appropriate stock concentration.
Prepare dilutions on experiment day by mixing to achieve concentrations of 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.5 µg/mL in sterile water.
For Mannitol, prepare a stock solution by dissolving an appropriate amount in sterile water to achieve the desired concentration.
Prepare dilutions on experiment day by mixing to achieve concentrations of 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 mg/mL in sterile water.
Dissolve a 5 mg bottle of Cytochalasin B into 25 mL of DMSO to achieve a stock concentration of 200 µg/mL.
Store the Cytochalasin B solution at -20°C for several months.
Add 1 mL of desired chemical, such as Mitomycin C, to 9 mL of cells in a T25 flask containing approximately 7-8x10^5 cells/mL.
For control samples, add 1 mL of sterile water instead of the chemical to the cell culture.
Place the flasks in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 3 hours.
Remove flasks from the incubator after 3 h.
Transfer cells to 15 mL polypropylene tubes.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 8 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and transfer cells to new T25 flasks containing a total of 10 mL of fresh culture medium.
Add 150 μL of Cytochalasin B stock (200 µg/mL) to each flask to achieve a final concentration of 3 µg/mL.
Return the flasks to the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator for a recovery time of 24 h.
Prepare 75 mM potassium chloride (KCl) by adding 2.79 g of KCl to 500 mL of ultrapure water.
Stir the 75 mM KCl solution for 5 min using a magnetic stirrer.
Sterilize the 75 mM KCl solution through a 200 μm filter.
Prepare 10 mL of 4% formalin by adding 4 mL of 10% formalin stock to 6 mL of 1x PBS without Ca²⁺ or Mg²⁺.
Store the 4% formalin at room temperature for several weeks.
Prepare 510 mL of wash buffer (2% FBS in 1X PBS) by adding 10 mL of FBS to a 500 mL bottle of 1x PBS.
Prepare 10 mL of a 100 μg/mL concentration of Hoechst 33342 by adding 100 µL of the stock concentration (1 mg/mL) to 9,900 µL of 1X PBS.
Store the Hoechst 33342 solution at 4 °C for several months.
Transfer all samples from flasks to 15 mL polypropylene tubes after the recovery period.
Centrifuge all samples at 200 x g for 8 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in each sample.
Add 5 mL of 75 mM KCl to each sample.
Mix gently by inversion three times.
Incubate the samples with 75 mM KCl at 4 °C for 7 min.
Add 2 mL of 4% formalin to each sample.
Mix gently by inversion three times.
Incubate the samples with 4% formalin at 4 °C for 10 min.
Centrifuge all samples at 200 x g for 8 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the samples in 100 µL of 4% formalin for 20 min.
Add 5 mL of wash buffer and centrifuge at 200 x g for 8 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the samples in 100 µL of wash buffer.
Transfer all samples to 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Perform a cell count on each sample to determine the number of cells per sample.
If necessary, dilute samples 1:100 in 1x PBS for accurate counting.
Add 5 µL of 100 µg/mL of reagent per 1x106 cells/mL to each sample.
Add 10 µL of 500 µg/mL of RNase per 100 µL of sample, achieving a final concentration of 50 µg/mL.
Incubate the samples at 37 °C in 5% CO2 for 30 min.
Micro-centrifuge all samples at 200 x g for 8 min.
Pipette to remove supernatant, leaving ~30 μL.
Resuspend all samples before running on the MIFC ensuring there are no bubbles in the tube.
Ensure the sheath, system calibration reagent, debubbler, cleanser, and sterilizer containers are full.
Empty the waste tank.
Power up the system.
Double-click on the MIFC software icon.
Click the Startup button.
Check the Start all calibrations and tests checkbox.
Flush the system.
Load sheath and system calibration reagents.
Calibrate the system.
Launch the MIFC data acquisition software.
Turn on the 405 nm laser.
Set the laser power to 10 mW.
Disable all other lasers, including SSC.
Set the BF to channels 1 and 9.
Confirm the magnification slider is set to 60x.
Select high-sensitivity mode.
Ensure only channels 1, 7, and 9 are showing in the image gallery.
Click on the Scatterplot icon.
Select All population.
Select Area M01 on the X-axis.
Select Aspect Ratio M01 on the Y-axis.
Click on the Square Region icon.
Draw a region around the single cells.
Name this region Single Cells.
Right-click on the plot and select Regions.
Highlight the Single Cells region.
Change the x-coordinates to 100 and 900.
Change the y-coordinates to 0.75 and 1.
Click on the Scatterplot icon.
Select Single Cells as the parent population.
Select Gradient RMS M01 on the X-axis and Gradient RMS M07 on the Y-axis.
Click on the Square Region icon and draw a region around the majority of the cells.
Name this region Focused Cells.
Right click on the plot and select Regions.
Highlight the Focused Cells region and change the x-coordinates to 55 and 75.
Change the y-coordinates to 9.5 and 20.
Click on the Histogram icon.
Select the Focused Cells population and select Intensity M07 as the feature.
Click on the Linear Region icon and draw a region across the main peak in the histogram.
Name this region DNA-positive.
Right click on the plot and select Regions.
Highlight the DNA-positive region and change the coordinates to 2 x 105 and 2 x 106.
Set the acquisition parameters.
Specify the file name and the destination folder.
Change the number of events to 20,000.
Select the DNA-positive population.
Click Load.
Place the control sample into the MIFC.
Click the Acquire button to collect the data.
Once the acquisition is complete, click the Return button to return the sample.
Remove the sample tube from the instrument.
Repeat this process for all remaining samples in the experiment.
Launch the MIFC analysis software package.
Click on Start Analysis to start the Open File Wizard.
Select a data file by browsing to the desired raw image file (.rif).
Click the Open button and click Next.
Since this is a single color assay, compensation is not necessary so click Next to bypass the compensation step.
At this stage there is no analysis template to apply, so click Next again.
If the analysis template has been downloaded from the supplementary material, select it now.
These templates only work with a 2 camera MIFC with BF set to channels 1 and 9 and nuclear imagery in channel 7 during acquisition.
Click Next.
Set the image display properties by selecting the 01 and 07.
Click Next.
It is very important to save the data analysis file (.daf) and the analysis template (.ast) often during sections 9–14 to avoid loss of progress.
Click on the Image Gallery Properties icon (blue/white icon).
In the Display Properties tab click Set Range to Pixel Data then change the color to yellow.
Click OK.
Create the non-apoptotic cells plot.
Click on the Analysis tab, then click Masks.
Click New, then click Function.
Under Function, choose Threshold.
Under Mask, choose M07.
Set the Intensity Percentage to 50.
Click OK.
Click OK again.
Click Close.
Click on the Analysis tab, then click Features.
Click New.
For the Feature Type, select Area.
For Mask, select the Threshold(M07,Ch07,50).
Click Set Default Name.
Click OK.
Click Close to start calculating the feature values.
Click on the Dot Plot icon.
Select the All population.
For the X-axis feature, choose the Contrast_M01_Ch01 feature.
For the Y-axis feature, choose Area_Threshold(M07,Ch07,50).
Click OK.
Click the Square Region button and draw a region around the majority of the cells.
Call this region Non-apoptotic.
Right click on the plot and click Regions.
Highlight the Non-apoptotic region.
Set the x-coordinates to 0 and 15.
Set the y-coordinates to 50 and 300.
Click Close.
Create the BNC mask (steps 9.3.1-9.3.5) to identify cells that contain only two nuclei.
Browse for a BNC in the image gallery and click on it.
This is to visualize creation of the mask in the Hoechst channel.
Click on the Analysis tab, then click Masks.
Click New, then click Function.
Under Function, choose LevelSet.
Under Mask, choose M07.
Select the Middle Level Mask radio button.
Set the Contour Detail Scale to 3.00.
Click OK.
Click OK again.
Click New.
Click Function.
Under Function, choose Dilate.
Under Mask, choose LevelSet(M07,Ch07,Middle,3).
Set the image to display to Ch07.
Set the Number of Pixels to 2.
Click OK.
Click OK again.
Click New.
Click Function.
Under Function, choose Watershed.
Under Mask, choose Dilate(LevelSet(M07,Ch07,Middle,3)2).
Set the image to display to Ch07.
Set the Line Thickness to 1.
Click OK.
Click OK again.
Click New.
Click Function.
Under Function, choose Range.
Under Mask, choose Watershed(Dilate(LevelSet(M07,Ch07,Middle,3)2)).
Set the image to display to Ch07.
Set the minimum and maximum area values to 115 and 5000, respectively.
Set the minimum and maximum aspect ratio values to 0.4 and 1, respectively.
Click OK.
In the Name field, change the text to read BNC.
Click OK.
Create the features and plots to obtain the final BNC population.
Spot Count BNC feature: Click on the Analysis tab.
Then Features.
Then New.
For the Feature Type, select Spot Count.
For Mask, select the final BNC mask created in 9.3.5.
Set the Connectedness to Four.
Change the name to Spot Count BNC.
Click OK.
Click Close to calculate the feature values.
Click the Histogram icon in Spot Count BNC histogram.
Select Non-apoptotic as the parent population.
Choose the Spot Count BNC feature for the X-axis.
Click OK.
Draw a region across bin 2 using the Linear Region icon.
Create the MN mask by browsing for a BNC that contains an MN in the image gallery.
Visualize creation of the MN mask in the Hoechst channel.
Click on the Analysis tab and then click Masks.
Create Spot Identification Mask 1: Click New, then click Function.
Under Function choose Spot and ensure Bright radio button is selected.
Under Mask choose M07, set Spot to Cell Background Ratio to 2.00.
Set Minimum Radius to 2 and Maximum Radius to 6.
Click OK twice.
Click New, then click Function.
Under Function choose Range, and under Mask choose LevelSet(M07,Ch07,Middle,3).
Set the Image to display Ch07.
Set Minimum and Maximum Area to 80 and 5000 respectively.
Set Minimum and Maximum Aspect Ratio to 0 and 1 respectively.
Click OK twice.
Click New, then click Function.
Under Function choose Dilate, under Mask choose Range(LevelSet(M07,Ch07,Middle,3),80-5000,0-1).
Set the Image to display Ch07.
Set Number of Pixels to 2.
Click OK twice.
Click New.
Double Click on the Spot(M07, Ch07, Bright, 2, 6, 2) mask to add it to the mask definition.
Click the And operator and then the Not operator.
Double click the Dilate(Range(LevelSet(M07, Ch07, Middle, 3), 80-5000, 0-1), 2) mask to add it to the mask definition.
Click OK.
Click New, then Function.
Under Function choose Range and under mask choose the mask created in 10.1.1.4.
Select Spot(M07, Ch07, Bright, 2, 6, 2) And Not Dilate(Range(LevelSet(M07, Ch07, Middle, 3), 80-5000, 0-1), 2).
Set the Image to Display to Ch07.
Set the Minimum and Maximum Area to 10 and 80, respectively.
Set the Minimum and Maximum Aspect Ratio to 0.4 and 1, respectively.
Click OK then OK again.
Spot identification mask 1 is complete.
Create masks, features and plots to identify the Mononucleated and Polynucleated populations.
Create the POLY mask.
Click Analysis, then Masks, then New then Function.
Under Function choose Range, under Mask choose Watershed(Dilate(LevelSet(M07, Ch07, Middle, 3), 2)).
Set the image to display to Ch07.
Set the Minimum and Maximum Area values to 135 and 5000, respectively.
Set the Minimum and Maximum Aspect Ratio values to 0.4 and 1, respectively.
Click OK.
In the Name field, change the text to read POLY then click OK then Close.
The Polynucleated cell mask is complete.
Click on the Analysis tab.
Then Masks, then New, then Function.
Under Function, select Component.
Under Mask, select the POLY mask.
For Ranking Feature, select Area.
For Sorting Order, click the Descending radio button.
Set Rank to 1.
Click OK.
Click OK again.
Repeat all steps except set Rank to 2 for creating POLY Component Masks 2.
Repeat all steps except set Rank to 3 for creating POLY Component Masks 3.
Repeat all steps except set Rank to 4 for creating POLY Component Masks 4.
Click the Analysis tab, then Features, then New.
For Feature Type, select Spot Count.
For Mask, choose the POLY mask and set the Connectedness at 4.
Click Set Default Name.
Click OK.
Close to calculate the feature values.
Click the Histogram icon.
Select the Non-apoptotic population.
For the X-axis feature, choose the Spot Count_POLY_4 feature.
Click on the Linear Region icon.
Draw a region across bin 1 on the histogram created in 11.3.2.
Call this region 1N.
Click on the Linear Region icon.
Draw a region across bin 3 on the histogram created in 11.3.2.
Call this region 3N.
Click on the Linear Region icon.
Draw a region across bin 4 on the histogram created in 11.3.2.
Call this region 4N.
Create the MONO Aspect Ratio Feature.
Click the Analysis tab, then Features, then New.
Under Feature Type, select the Aspect Ratio feature.
Under Mask, select Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending).
Click Set Default Name.
Click OK.
Click New under Feature Type in the Feature Manager window.
Select Circularity feature.
Under Mask, select Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending).
Click Set Default Name.
Click OK.
Click Close to calculate the feature values.
Click the Dot Plot icon.
Select 1N as the parent population.
For the X Axis Feature, choose Circularity_Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending).
For the Y Axis Feature, choose Aspect Ratio_Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending).
Click OK.
Click the Square Region button.
Draw a region around the cell population towards the top right portion of the plot.
Name this region Circular_1N.
Right click on the plot and click Regions.
Highlight the Circular_1N region.
Change the X Coordinates to 20 and 55.
Change the Y Coordinates to 0.85 and 1.0.
Click Close.
Create the Area POLY/Area_M07 feature.
Click the Analysis tab.
Select Features from the menu, then New.
Under Feature Type, select the Area feature.
Under Mask, select Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending).
Click Set Default Name.
Click OK.
With the Feature Manager window still open, click New.
Click the Combined radio button under Feature Type.
Highlight the Area_Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending) and click the down arrow to add it to the feature definition.
Click the division symbol (/).
Select the Area_M07 feature and click the down arrow to add it to the feature definition.
Click Set Default Name.
Click OK.
Click Close to start calculating the feature values.
For the final MONO population dot plot, click the dot plot icon.
Select Circular_1N as the parent population.
Choose Aspect Ratio_M07 for the X Axis Feature.
Choose Area_Component(1, Area, POLY, Descending) / Area_M07 for the Y Axis Feature.
Click OK.
Click the Square Region button and draw a region around the majority of the cells.
Name this region Mononucleated.
Right click on the plot and click Regions.
Highlight the Mononucleated region.
Change the X Coordinates to 0.85 and 1.0.
Change the Y Coordinates to 0.55 and 1.0.
Click Close.
Click on the Image Gallery Properties button.
Click on the View tab.
Click on the Composites tab.
Click New.
Under Name type Ch01/Ch07.
Click Add Image.
Under Image choose Ch01 and set the Percent to 100.
Click Add Image again.
Under Image choose Ch07 and set the Percent to 100.
Click New.
Under Name type BNC and MN masks.
Click Add Column.
Under Image Type choose Ch01 and under Mask choose None.
Click Add Column.
Under Image Type choose Ch07 and under Mask choose None.
Click Add Column.
Under Image Type choose Ch07 and under Mask choose BNC.
Click Add Column.
Under Image Type choose Ch07 and under Mask choose MN mask.
The Ch01/Ch07 composite image should be automatically added to the view.
Click OK to close the Image Gallery Properties window.
Create a custom view to examine the POLY mask.
Click on the Reports tab then click Define Statistics Report.
In the new window, click Add Columns.
Add the BNC count statistic.
Under Statistics select Count and under Selected Population choose the BNCs population.
Click Add Statistics to add the statistic to the list.
Repeat step 14.2 to create separate columns for the MN BNCs, MONO, TRI and POLY populations.
Click Close then click OK.
Save the data analysis template as a new file using File, Save As Template.
Batch process experiment files using the saved data analysis template.
Click Add Batch under Tools menu and then click Add Files to select experiment files (.rif).
Select the appropriate data analysis template file (.ast or .daf) in the browse window.
Preview Statistics Report button to check if proper template is selected.
Close the preview statistics report window after verification.
Submit batches for processing all selected files simultaneously.
Calculate genotoxicity by dividing the number of cells in the MN BNCs population by the number of cells in the BNCs population then multiplying by 100.
Sum the number of TRI and QUAD cells to determine the total number of POLY cells.
Calculate the Cytokinesis-Block Proliferation Index (CBPI) using the number of MONO, BNCs, and POLY cells.
Calculate the cytotoxicity for each culture using CBPI values from control cultures (C) and chemically exposed cultures (T).
